chain.text: Mont Ventoux observatory runs a 60-cm reflector (2017) and a 20-cm outreach refractor, averaging 195 useful nights yearly (168 in 2024). Monthly data (~400 GB) transfers nightly to Marseille in 40 minutes. A new main camera (March 2025) has 30% lower read noise but needs a full-night offline firmware update. Past incidents: a 2023 dome motor seizure bent a counterweight rod (fixed, limit switch added); a February 2025 timestamp offset lost three weeks of photometry (now GPS-checked each session). Rules: no observing during outreach, raw frames compressed only after two years, software changes need a test night. A proposed Spanish collaboration awaits evaluation of its scheduling tool and network capacity.

**Handover summary — Mont Ventoux Observatory**

The site runs a 60-cm reflector (2017) and a 20-cm outreach refractor. Useful nights average 195/year (168 in 2024, wet autumn). About 400 GB/month is archived nightly to a Marseille university server; the transfer takes 40 minutes. The main camera was replaced in March 2025 (30% lower read noise) and needs a full-night offline firmware update. Two incidents: a 2023 dome motor seizure bent a counterweight rod (repaired, limit switch added), and a February 2025 timestamp offset lost three weeks of photometry (now GPS-checked each session). Rules: no observing during outreach; raw frames compressed only after two years; software changes need a test night. A Spanish collaboration awaits evaluation of scheduling tool and network capacity.

**Gaps:** E01 (handover/instrument context) and E06 (incident list framing) are not covered.
